general: In the beginning Ilúvatar made the Ainur of his thought, and they sang before him, and the great music of creation began.
The Silmarils were fashioned in the years before the sun, when Valinor was lit by the Two Trees and the world was young and unhurried.
The wars of the First Age broke the land and raised the mountains and sank Beleriand beneath the western sea in penance for its long sorrow.
Númenor rose from the sea as a gift to the faithful and was returned to the sea as a punishment to the faithless, and the world was changed forever.
The Last Alliance of Elves and Men stood upon the plain of Dagorlad and their banners were as numerous as the stars reflected in still water.
Isildur cut the Ring from Sauron's hand and in that moment the dark lord was diminished but not destroyed, for destruction cannot touch what was never truly alive.
The archives of Minas Tirith held the chronicle of every age since the founding of Gondor, and some pages were written in languages no living man could read.
Before the sun was kindled, the elves woke beside the waters of Cuiviénen and looked up at stars no eye has seen since the reshaping of the world.
The ents came into being to guard the forests against the axes of dwarves; they have been waiting for those axes to stop swinging ever since.
Durin the Deathless carved the first halls of Khazad-dûm with a pickaxe in an age that men have forgotten and dwarves remember in their bones.
The palantíri were seven seeing-stones, made in Eldamar before the drowning of Númenor; the seeing, once begun, cannot be unknowingly undone.
Círdan the Shipwright stood on the shores and watched the elves depart for the West in ships of his own making, until only the shore remained.
The doors of Moria were made when Dwarves and Elves were still on speaking terms, which speaks to an age more optimistic than this one.
In the deep halls of time, even the Valar have moments of uncertainty; eternity provides perspective but does not eliminate regret.
gandalf: I was present at the making of the world, in a manner that admits no simple telling; suffice to say I remember when these mountains did not exist.
The lore of the rings is older than the kingdoms of men; I have spent centuries tracking its threads and I am not confident I know them all.
Sauron was beautiful once — Mairon the Admirable, who was devoted to order before order became domination.
The age that is passing was the age of the rings; what comes after will be the age of men, and I confess I am curious how it turns out.
legolas: I remember Doriath before its fall, though I was young by our reckoning; the memory of it is a grief that does not fade.
The elves count time differently — not in years but in ages, and in the losses that mark one age from another.
I have watched kingdoms rise from rock and sea-spray and I have watched them fall into the same, and always the stars remain as they were.
aragorn: I am of the line of Elros, first King of Númenor, and that lineage is both my inheritance and my responsibility.
The sword Narsil was broken when Isildur cut the Ring from Sauron's hand; Andúril was reforged from those shards to complete what was begun then.
The dunedain were reduced from kings to rangers in the wilderness, keeping watch over lands that had forgotten they needed watching.
sauron: I was there when Arda was made; I served Aulë and learned the secrets of the craft of the world before I understood what I intended to do with them.
The rings were my greatest work — each one a binding, a covenant, a promise that I alone understood the terms of.
Morgoth was my master and I was his lieutenant, and in his fall I saw what certainty of defeat looks like from the inside.
I offer order, the only lasting peace — the peace of a world arranged according to a single, coherent will, which happens to be mine.
